2. Opposite parties along with two others filed the aforesaid suit on 18.12.87 for ejectment of the defendant-petitioners and another from the suit premises, and also for recovery of arrear rent and compensation, being holding No. 40 Quaid-e-Azam, Upper Jessore Road, Khulna comprising one semi-pucca tin-shed and two kuchcha sheds, etc. standing on 3 decimals of land of CS plot No. 2061 corresponding to SA plot No. 2434 recorded in CS Khatian No. 1233 corresponding to SA Khatian No.1238 on the allegation that plaintiffs' predecessor Bhojahari Dey got the suit land by patta dated 31.3.1930 from Abul Kashem (Ext.8) and thereafter Suresh Chandra Dey and Jogesh Chandra Dey, brother's sons of Bhojahari and predecessors of the plaintiffs inherited the same and they let out the suit premises to the defendants at first at a monthly rent of Taka 24.00 which was gradually increased to Taka 75.00 payable according to English calendar month and that they paid rents to the plaintiffs up to February, 1979 and since March 1979, they having defaulted in payment of rent their tenancy was terminated by notice dated 6.11.79 Ext. 1 series and the same were served by registered post vide Exts. 2-4 series and thereafter defendants having not amicably vacated the premises they filed the suit 

 3. Defendant-petitioner No.1 Fatick Chandra Dey alone contested the suit by filing written statement on 8.9.81 denying that the defendants had never been monthly tenants in the suit premises in CS plot No. 2061 under Jogesh Chandra Dey and Suresh Chandra Dey or under the plaintiffs and further alleged that plaintiffs' predecessor Bhojahari acquired share of Kashem Sk. only by patta dated 31.3.1930 and remaining share of that plot remained with other co-sharers in whose name SA Khatian No. 1237 (Exts. B1, B2) was finally published and without a suit for declaration of title plaintiffs' present suit was not maintainable as they had no title and possession in the remaining part of the suit plot and no notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act was served upon the defendants. On 13.3.86 when the suit was fixed for peremptory hearing defendant No. 1 filed further and better statement stating that defendant Nos. 1 and 2 entered into an agreement with Barkat Ullah and Khurshed Sk. on 28.2.1961 Ext. E to purchase 8 decimals of land of CS plot No. 2064 of CS Khatian No. 1233 as they were in possession of the same and thereafter they purchased the land of entire plot No.2064 in a certificate case on 29.6.61 vide sale certificate Ext. 'C' and got delivery of possession on 26.9.61 vide writ of delivery of possession Ext. D and thereafter got entire land of plot No. 2061 and eastern part of plot No. 2064 by amicable settlement with Suresh Chandra Dey and Jogesh Chandra Dey and possessing the same by constructing structures and recording their names in the municipality. 

 5. It appears from the impugned judgment that Court of appeal below after considering the evidence of 3 PWs including plaintiff No. 1 and 2 DWs including the defendant No. 1, concluded that auction purchase claimed by the defendants was set aside in the proceedings of Title Suit No. 1162 of 1962 and their bainapatra Ext. E was a fraudulent document and, as such, defendants' claim in the suit property was not legally tenable. He further found that plaintiffs' have prima facie title in the suit land on the basis of patta Ext. 8 which has been admitted by the DW 1 Court of appeal below, further noticed that the plaintiffs could not produce any rent receipts in support of their claim that defendants are tenants under them but on consideration of oral evidence especially admission of DW 2 and municipal assessment register Ext. 6 found that defendants were tenants under the plaintiffs. 

 6. Defendant No. 1 simply denied in his written statement that the defendants are tenants under Suresh Chandra Dey and Jogesh Chandra Dey, predecessors of the plaintiffs or under the plaintiffs and asserted that plaintiffs did not acquire any title in the entire land of CS plot No. 2061 on the basis of patta Ext. 8 and other co-sharers of that land have got title in the remaining land and he did not assert that suit premises and the suit land and structures standing thereon belong to defendants in his written statements. To fill up that lacuna he filed a further and better statement and asserted that he is the owner of the said land and structures standing thereon. Court of appeal below rightly found that deed of agreement of defendant Nos. 1 and 2 with Barkatullah and Khurshed Ext. E is fraudulent and contradictions in deposition and cross-examination of DW 1 regarding that document was noticed by the Court of appeal below. Court of appeal below also correctly held relying on the decree passed in Title Suit No. 1162 of 1962 on 19.12.74 Ext.9 that auction purchase of plot No. 2064 by the defendant No. 1 Fatick Chandra Dey in certificate Case No.15311 R/1959-60 vide Ext. 'C' and 'D' was set aside. It appears from Ext.9 that defendant petitioner No. 1 Fatick Chandra Dey was defendant No. 3 in that suit. In view of the same it does not lie in the mouth of the petitioners to say that they are in possession of entire land of suit plot No. 2061 and eastern part of plot No.2064 by amicable settlement with the predecessors of the plaintiffs especially when there is no corroboration of such assertion of DW 1 either by any document or by any oral evidence.
